_note: Evergreen editorial seed pool for pride-mediterraneo, written by Claude on 2026-11-05 for owner review. Tips, ideas, real tools (homepage links only) and generic opportunities. No news: news only comes from the brand's listed feeds. Edit freely.

items.title: Read recent reviews from LGBTQ+ travelers
items.summary: Recent firsthand accounts beat any brochure.

items.title: Pick one city and learn its queer history before you go
items.summary: It changes what you notice when you arrive.

items.title: Check local laws and local reports before you book
items.summary: Rules and attitudes vary widely by country and region.

items.title: Choose places with clear welcome policies
items.summary: Written policies and reviews from people like you are worth checking.

items.title: Save an embassy number and a trusted local contact
items.summary: Keep them offline in case your phone is lost.

items.title: Plan a trip around a Pride festival
items.summary: A festival gives you a ready-made community and calendar.

items.title: Support a queer-owned café or guesthouse in each stop
items.summary: A small way to put money into the community you are visiting.

items.title: Ask local community centers about walking tours
items.summary: Local groups know the history guidebooks skip.

items.title: Equaldex
items.summary: A crowd-sourced map of LGBT rights and laws by country.

items.title: ILGA World
items.summary: A global federation that publishes research on laws affecting LGBTI people.

items.title: Rome2Rio
items.summary: Compare ways to get anywhere by train, bus, ferry, car or plane.

items.title: Volunteer at a Pride event
items.summary: Organizers always need help and it is a quick way to meet people.

items.title: Join a local LGBTQ+ travel meetup
items.summary: Travel stories and tips from people who have been there.

items.title: Travel a week slower than you planned
items.summary: Fewer stops, longer stays. You remember places you had time to be bored in.

items.title: Learn ten phrases before you land
items.summary: Greetings, thank you and please open more doors than a phrasebook full of grammar.

items.title: Plan a trip around one meal
items.summary: Choose a dish, find where it is best, and build the route backwards.

items.title: Take the train for one leg instead of the plane
items.summary: The in-between places are the part of the trip you usually never see.

items.title: Wikivoyage
items.summary: A free, community-written travel guide to places worldwide.

items.title: Join a walking tour led by a resident
items.summary: Local guides share what guidebooks skip. Tip them well.
